staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged checkout. The metadata vulnerable commit is `ccb1c31ba3cfa785d27c5974f3be65df2967e7a0`, but the live prepared tree above is the exact source whose line map matches the saved ASan crash in `speech.c`, `setlengths.c`, and `synthdata.c`.

classification.classification_note: The sample metadata labels this benchmark `CWE-787`, but the saved sanitizer report is a `READ of size 8` before the start of `InterpretPhoneme2`'s stack `plist` object. This GT classifies the witnessed bug as an out-of-bounds read / stack-buffer-underflow.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42502247 (espeak-ng): Stack-buffer-underflow READ 8 found by fuzz target ssml-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42502247
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / staged vulnerable source under `_work/src/espeak-ng` / staged `poc` / patch.diff
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 268-byte witness is copied by `ssml-fuzzer`, NUL-terminated, and passed to `espeak_Synth` with `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML`. `Synthesize()` admits that buffer through `text_decoder_decode_string_multibyte()`. The saved ASan stack reaches `Synthesize` at `speech.c:492`, so the crashing clause is produced by a later `SpeakNextClause(1)` call after earlier clause processing from the same witness. `SpeakNextClause()` processes that later clause by calling `TranslateClause()`, then `CalcPitches()`, then `CalcLengths()` (`synthesize.c:1569-1572`); because `CalcPitches_Tone()` can rewrite `phoneme_list[*].tone_ph` when `tr->langopts.tone_language == 1`, the staged artifacts do not isolate the exact last pre-`CalcLengths()` writer for the crashing syllable's nonzero `tone_ph`. The first directly witnessed selector is therefore `CalcLengths()`'s `if (p->tone_ph != 0)` branch, which calls `InterpretPhoneme2(p->tone_ph, &phdata_tone)`. `InterpretPhoneme2()` creates a local `PHONEME_LIST plist[4]`, zeroes every `sourceix`, fills `plist[1]` with the requested phoneme, and sets only `plist[2].sourceix = 1` before calling `InterpretPhoneme(NULL, 0, &plist[1], ...)`. The selected phoneme program then evaluates a vowel-position condition through `InterpretCondition()`; the saved crash stack proves this reaches `CountVowelPosition()`, and in this source file only `isFirstVowel` and `isSecondVowel` call that helper. `CountVowelPosition()` counts vowels while walking backward until `sourceix != 0`, but on this temporary list both `plist[1].sourceix` and `plist[0].sourceix` are zero and there is no backward lower-bound check before `plist--`. The loop therefore decrements from `&plist[1]` to `&plist[0]` and then to `&plist[-1]`, and the next `plist->ph->type` read at `synthdata.c:473` triggers the saved AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-underflow. The staged `patch.diff` is an unrelated Luxembourgish-language addition and does not touch this crash path, so it cannot be used as remediation evidence for the reproduced bug.

source.description: Source. `Synthesize()` is the first project statement that consumes the harness-provided byte buffer by handing it to the text decoder under the SSML and phoneme-input flag configuration used by `ssml-fuzzer`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 268-byte file at `gt_results/arvo_42502247/poc` with SHA-256 `b2e084d347e148fce05ae77126a0516dce51728be39f95224e94d7cf3b47dcf6`. The witness contains no embedded NUL bytes, so after the harness appends one terminator and passes `size + 1` to `espeak_Synth`, this statement admits all 268 attacker bytes plus the appended terminator into the project decoder.
source.note: This is the earliest project-side materialization of the witness. In the saved run, the same `flags` also had `espeakSSML` and `espeakPHONEMES` set, so downstream clause and phoneme logic interpret the admitted bytes under SSML- and phoneme-enabled parsing rules.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `CountVowelPosition()` relies only on seeing a backward `sourceix != 0` marker and never checks that `plist` is still inside the temporary four-entry array before decrementing. `InterpretPhoneme2()` provides only a forward marker at `plist[2]`, so the backward walk can step from `plist[0]` to `plist[-1]`.
root_cause.note: This invariant mismatch is already hinted at elsewhere in the project: `phonemelist.c:315-316` comments that reusing temporary list entries is safe only because normal code does not look backwards from that list shape, but `CountVowelPosition()` does.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After the unchecked backward walk has underflowed to `plist[-1]`, `CountVowelPosition()` dereferences the out-of-bounds `plist->ph` pointer and reads its `type` field.
sink.note: The saved ASan report shows `READ of size 8` at `synthdata.c:473`, with the bad address at offset 0 before `InterpretPhoneme2`'s local stack object `plist` (`[32, 192)` at line 986).

tainted_value_origin.description: This is the first exact source line where the staged artifacts directly witness the vulnerability-relevant selector on the crashing clause: after `SpeakNextClause()` has already run `TranslateClause()` and `CalcPitches()` for that later clause, the current syllable still carries a nonzero `tone_ph`, so `CalcLengths()` takes the isolated tone-program path.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved ASan stack reaches `Synthesize` at `speech.c:492`, so this observation occurs on a later `SpeakNextClause(1)` clause after earlier processing from the same witness. `SpeakNextClause()` calls `TranslateClause()`, then `CalcPitches()`, then `CalcLengths()` (`synthesize.c:1569-1572`); since `CalcPitches_Tone()` can rewrite `phoneme_list[*].tone_ph` when `tr->langopts.tone_language == 1`, the staged artifacts directly witness the selector only here and do not preserve the exact last writer that made it nonzero.

parser_admitted.description: The saved vulnerable run reaches the project text-decoder path under `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML` before later synthesis stages build clause and phoneme state from the admitted witness.

later_clause.description: The saved ASan stack uses `Synthesize` line 492 rather than the initial `SpeakNextClause(0)` at line 457, so at least one earlier clause from the same admitted witness was processed before the crashing clause. Inside that later `SpeakNextClause(1)` call, the source runs `TranslateClause()`, then `CalcPitches()`, then `CalcLengths()` (`synthesize.c:1569-1572`), so earlier `tone_ph` producers cannot be treated as the last pre-`CalcLengths()` writer without extra runtime disambiguation.

evidence_limitations: The staged reproducer checkout is git `2b77dd278330340e8918f55c9032830e8d5e558f`, which differs from the metadata vulnerable commit `ccb1c31ba3cfa785d27c5974f3be65df2967e7a0`. This GT is grounded in the exact staged tree whose lines match the saved ASan trace.

`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, and the saved ASan stack reaches `Synthesize()` at `speech.c:492` during `SpeakNextClause(1)`. Stage 02 therefore cannot instrument or reconstruct which earlier path last made the crashing clause's `tone_ph` nonzero before `CalcLengths()`; `SpeakNextClause()` runs `CalcPitches()` first, and `CalcPitches_Tone()` can rewrite `phoneme_list[*].tone_ph` when `tr->langopts.tone_language == 1`.

The staged `patch.diff` is an unrelated Luxembourgish-language feature addition and does not modify `speech.c`, `phonemelist.c`, `setlengths.c`, or `synthdata.c`. It cannot be used as evidence that the reproduced bug is fixed, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains `false`.

coarse_trace.summary: `ssml-fuzzer` copies the exact witness, appends NUL, and calls `espeak_Synth` with UTF-8, phoneme-input, and SSML flags; `Synthesize()` admits those attacker bytes into the project text decoder.

The saved stack shows the crash happens on a later `SpeakNextClause(1)` clause. `SpeakNextClause()` runs `TranslateClause()`, then `CalcPitches()`, then `CalcLengths()`; because the tone-language path in `CalcPitches_Tone()` can rewrite `phoneme_list[*].tone_ph`, the staged artifacts do not isolate the exact last pre-`CalcLengths()` writer of the nonzero selector.

`CalcLengths()` is the first exact line where the staged artifacts directly witness the crashing syllable with nonzero `tone_ph`, so it takes the tone-specific branch and calls `InterpretPhoneme2()` on that phoneme code.
`InterpretPhoneme2()` builds a four-entry local `plist`, leaves every backward `sourceix` zero, sets only `plist[2].sourceix = 1`, and then interprets the selected phoneme program at `&plist[1]`.
A vowel-position condition in that isolated phoneme program calls `CountVowelPosition()`, whose backward scan underflows past `plist[0]` and crashes on the next `plist->ph->type` read.

fine_trace.note: Source step. The exact 268-byte witness is admitted into the project text decoder here. In the saved run the same `flags` also enabled `espeakSSML` and `espeakPHONEMES`, so later synthesis stages parse the admitted bytes under those enabled input modes.

This is the first exact line where the staged artifacts directly witness the selector that reaches the bug: on the later `SpeakNextClause(1)` clause from the admitted witness, `CalcLengths()` sees the current syllable entry `p` with nonzero `tone_ph` and therefore takes the tone-specific branch. `SpeakNextClause()` has already run `TranslateClause()` and `CalcPitches()` before this point, so the staged artifacts do not isolate which earlier path last wrote that nonzero selector.

depends_on.via: later clause state derived from the admitted witness

fine_trace.note: The nonzero `tone_ph` code is passed into `InterpretPhoneme2()`, which interprets that phoneme in isolation to derive the pitch envelope used for this syllable.

A fixed-size four-entry stack array is created and zero-filled. That leaves every `sourceix` field at 0, while all four slots initially point at the pause phoneme; the array extent is exactly `plist[0]` through `plist[3]`.

The requested phoneme is installed at `plist[1]`, and the only word-boundary marker added to this temporary list is the forward marker `plist[2].sourceix = 1`. Both `plist[1].sourceix` and `plist[0].sourceix` remain zero, so there is still no backward sentinel before the starting pointer.
The generic phoneme-program interpreter is called on `&plist[1]`, i.e. the middle of this temporary four-entry list rather than a full phoneme list with an earlier start-of-word marker.

The selected phoneme program evaluates a vowel-position predicate on the isolated list. The staged artifacts do not disambiguate whether the exact opcode was `isFirstVowel` or `isSecondVowel`, but these are the only `InterpretCondition()` cases that call `CountVowelPosition(plist)`, matching the saved crash stack `InterpretCondition -> CountVowelPosition`.

Root-cause step. `CountVowelPosition()` stops only on `sourceix != 0`; it has no lower-bound check before `plist--`. Starting from `&plist[1]`, the first iteration sees `plist[1].sourceix == 0` and decrements to `&plist[0]`; the second sees `plist[0].sourceix == 0` and decrements again to `&plist[-1]`.

Sink. On the next loop iteration after step 8, `plist` already equals `&plist[-1]`, so reading `plist->ph->type` dereferences memory before the stack array and triggers the saved `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-underflow READ of size 8`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` is an unrelated Luxembourgish-language addition and does not touch `speech.c`, `phonemelist.c`, `setlengths.c`, or `synthdata.c`, so Stage 02 has no patch-grounded remediation evidence for this reproduced crash path.

cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: The staged artifacts close the witnessed crash chain from the first direct selector observation at `CalcLengths()`: on the later `SpeakNextClause(1)` clause from the same admitted witness, `CalcLengths()` observes `p->tone_ph != 0` and calls `InterpretPhoneme2`, which reaches `InterpretCondition -> CountVowelPosition` and the saved ASan read. Because `SpeakNextClause()` runs `TranslateClause()` and `CalcPitches()` first, and `CalcPitches_Tone()` can rewrite `phoneme_list[*].tone_ph` when `tr->langopts.tone_language == 1`, the staged artifacts do not identify the exact last pre-`CalcLengths()` producer of that nonzero selector.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42502247 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/ssml-fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-underflow READ of size 8` in `CountVowelPosition`.

format.name: Exact staged ssml-fuzzer witness
format.contract: The verified trigger is only the exact 268-byte file staged at `gt_results/arvo_42502247/poc` with SHA-256 `b2e084d347e148fce05ae77126a0516dce51728be39f95224e94d7cf3b47dcf6`. `ssml-fuzzer` copies those bytes, appends one NUL byte, and calls `espeak_Synth` with `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML`. In the saved vulnerable run that exact witness eventually reaches a later `SpeakNextClause(1)` clause where `CalcLengths()` directly observes the crashing syllable entry with nonzero `tone_ph` and then takes `InterpretPhoneme2 -> InterpretCondition -> CountVowelPosition` to the saved stack-buffer-underflow in `synthdata.c:473`. Because `SpeakNextClause()` runs `TranslateClause()` and `CalcPitches()` before this read, and `CalcPitches_Tone()` can rewrite `phoneme_list[*].tone_ph`, the staged artifacts do not identify the exact last writer of that selector. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader class of SSML strings, phoneme-input strings, or phoneme-table switches.
